newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac makes offer for Bank Melbourne.
newsitem.headline: Westpac makes offer for Bank Melbourne.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Thursday it planned to merge with Bank of Melbourne Ltd via a scheme of arrangement which values the Victorian-based bank at A$1.435 billion.

Westpac said under the offer, converting preference sahreholders will have a choice of A$15.36 cash for each converting preference share or a combination of Westpac shares and cash to an equivalent value of A$15.36, with the maximum cash component being A$1.36 for each converting share.
It said converting preference sharehlders would also be paid the May 31 fully franked dividend of 39 cents per share.
Stewart said Bank of Melbourne shareholders did not need to take any immediate action in respect of the proposed merger, as shareholders would be sent the mergr details in a few weeks.
Westpac said the special dividend is fully franked.
Stewart said the Westpac offer is a multiple of 15.2 times 1997 prospective earnings forecast by Barcep.
This represented 2.1 times net assets which was comparable to the 2.1 times net assets paid by St George Bank Ltd for Advance Bank and the 2.1 times net assets paid by Westpac for Challenge.

He said on the completion of the offer Bank of Melbourne would continue with its own chief executive officer, who will be responsible for the day-to-day combined retail operations of both Bank of Melbourne and Westpac.
Westpac said Stewart would be invited to join the Westpac board, and Westpac managing director Bob Joss and another senior Westpac executive would join the Bank of Melbourne board.
The A$9.75 per share offer represented a premium of 20.4 percent to Bank of Melbourne's share price one month prior to the announcement, Bank of Melbourne said.
Bank of Melbourne requested a halt to trading in its shares on Wednesday after the stock soared 65 cents to A$8.80.
While Westpac shares fell 23.7 cents to A$6.873 on Wednesday as rumours spread that the bank was to make an offer for the Bnak of Melbourne. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
